Jackfruit: A handsome evergreen tree with glossy leaves up to 20 m tall in ideal conditions. Cultivated for its misshapen fruits - largest edible fruit in the world
Mango: Semi-evergreen trees with long, glossy leaves that can grow up to 35 m in favourable sites. Bark is grey-brown and rough with shallow cracks.
Tamarind: Large, handsome, long-lived tree with a squat trunk and a shady crown. Introduced to India from E Africa, but virtually indigenous. The bark is dark grey, rough with shallow fissures

Jackfruit: Male and female separate, on the same tree. Male flowers tiny, in clusters emerging from new branchlets; female flowers densely crowded on old branches or directly from the trunk
Mango: Mango flowers are tiny, yellowish-green, strongly scented, in huge, branched clusters. Most flowers are male and the rest bisexual.
Tamarind: Small, with 3 unequal-sized yellow petals veined with red; flower cup has 4 creamy segments

Jackfruit: Gigantic, lumpy, barrel- or pear-shaped; pollinated by small flies and beetles
Mango: Fruit is smooth-skinned, waxy and in various colours depending on the variety. Flesh is fibrous or pulpy and the stone flattened, kidney-shaped
Tamarind: Beanlike pod bulging over the seeds, up to 20 cm long; green at first, ripening cinnamon-brown. Young pod is covered with a downy felt.
